subject: Next steps: deployment routing & compliance evidence for HealthPrime (post-demo)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@healthprime.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@healthprime.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: deployment routing & compliance evidence for HealthPrime (post-demo)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet earlier today — thanks for walking through your primary workflows and the PHI use cases. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have a shared plan: 

Call recap (high level)
- HealthPrime will process PHI for patient triage and document summarization; expected steady-state QPS ~ 60 rps with spikes during business hours.
- Key compliance asks: BAA in place, SOC 2 artifacts for the last 6 months, encryption at-rest key management details, and audit log retention policy.
- Initial hosting preference: you indicated Dedicated capacity is preferred, but Private VPC is possible if procurement requires explicit network isolation.

Recommended next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (security + infra team) — 60 minutes to validate runtime architecture, network flows, and key management.
2) We’ll prepare a targeted evidence bundle (SOC 2 summary + relevant artifacts, BAA draft) and a short matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC for your PHI scenarios.
3) Procurement questions: Priya / IT to confirm required PO/contract timeline and if DocuSign BAA is acceptable.

Attachments I’m including: HealthPrime_BAA_Reqs.xlsx (your spreadsheet from the call), Redwood_SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf (summary + artifact list), HealthPrime_Procurement_Questions.docx (procurement checklist).

Can you confirm availability for a technical call Thursday or Friday (we have slots 10:00–12:00 PT and 15:00–17:00 PT)? Also confirm whether Dedicated capacity is the default route or if you need us to price Private VPC in the same packet.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-03-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment routing & compliance evidence for HealthPrime (post-demo)

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: PHI will be processed. Our legal & security teams require a signed BAA before production. Procurement also wants to see SOC 2 Type II evidence for the past 6 months.
- Preferred route: Dedicated capacity seems like the right balance of control and cost for now. If procurement insists on network-level isolation, we will evaluate Private VPC, but that will stretch timelines.
- Specific evidence asks from security: SOC 2 report summary (scope & last audit date), encryption at-rest (who manages keys? customer KMS or Redwood-managed KMS), key rotation policy, and sample audit logs showing per-token request tracing/retention.

Procurement contact: it@healthprime.com (please loop them on pricing/contract). Our target go/no-go: mid-April; budget is provisionally approved but contingent on SLA and evidence.

Alex Hoffman
Head of Platform Engineering | HealthPrime
alex.hoffman@healthprime.com

Date: 2027-03-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment routing & compliance evidence for HealthPrime (post-demo)

Ben / Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks — below is a pragmatic path we typically follow for PHI customers and what we can provide this week: 

Recommended path (two-track):
1) Primary: Dedicated capacity (recommended)
   - Benefits: GPU-reserved pool, predictable throughput, data isolation at tenancy level, faster onboarding (3–4 weeks typical for standard dedicated).
   - What we’ll provide immediately: SOC 2 summary + attestation cover letter, sample audit logs (redacted), KMS integration guide, and a BAA draft.

2) If procurement requires: Private VPC / On-prem package
   - Benefits: Full network isolation, can run in your VPC or on-prem.
   - Trade-offs: Longer lead time (6–10 weeks depending on network approvals), higher engineering effort and on-boarding support.

Preliminary evidence bundle we can deliver (this week)
- Redwood_SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf — scope, last audit date, controls mapped to data flows.
- Sample per-request audit logs (redacted) — timeframe: last 30 days.
- KMS options: customer-managed KMS (preferred for PHI) or Redwood-managed with HSM-backed keys.
- BAA draft (to be redlined by your legal team) — we’ll prepare DocuSign-ready version once procurement confirms.

Action items I’ll take (Marissa):
- Prepare a one-page comparison table (Dedicated vs Private VPC) with timelines & cost delta.
- Pull SOC 2 artifact list and work with security to add any extra items Alex requested.
- Coordinate with Rishi for SLA & pricing exceptions if needed.

Ben — I can join the technical deep-dive. Proposed times (PT): Thu 2027-03-25 10:30 or Fri 2027-03-26 15:00. Which works for you/HealthPrime?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com

Proposed immediate steps
- Technical deep-dive: Thu 2027-03-25 10:30 PT (Marissa & Rishi will join). I’ll send the calendar invite in the next 30 minutes.
- Evidence packet: you should see the SOC 2 summary + sample logs + BAA draft by end of day Friday (2027-03-26).
- Procurement loop: Marissa / I will include it@healthprime.com on the pricing packet and request expected PO timing.

Will follow up with the invite and links. Appreciate the speedy alignment — we’ll be ready to move fast if procurement gives the green light.
